summary: This note extrapolates the future of Earth from long-term influences: surface chemistry, interior cooling, gravitational interactions in the Solar System, and the Sun's steadily rising luminosity, with human technology as a major uncertainty. It covers the biotic crisis, celestial threats such as comet impacts and nearby supernovae, Milankovitch glaciation cycles, orbit and obliquity changes, plate tectonics and supercontinents, core solidification, the Sun's evolution, and the long decline of plant and animal life. The source text is cut off mid-section.
one_line: Scientific projections of Earth's long-term biological and geological future, from human-driven extinction and celestial hazards to the Sun's evolution and the eventual loss of life.
key_facts: The current Holocene extinction is being caused by technology, and its effects may last for up to five million years.
An estimated 10% of the total species had been lost as of 2007, and about 30% of species are at risk of extinction in the next hundred years.
Humans use about 20% of global primary production, and the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased by close to 50% since the start of the Industrial Revolution.
An impact from an asteroid or comet with a diameter of 5-10 km or larger can create a global environmental disaster and lower land temperatures by about 15 °C within a week.
Within the Milky Way, supernova explosions occur on average once every 40 years.
A supernova explosion at a distance of 26 light-years will reduce the ozone column density by half.
Earth's orbit is likely to remain dynamically stable for billions of years, and in all 1,600 simulations the semimajor axis, eccentricity, and inclination remained nearly constant.
Earth is passing through the quaternary glaciation and is presently in the Holocene interglacial period, which would normally be expected to end in about 25,000 years.
The Moon's tidal effects are expected to increase the length of the day by more than 1.5 hours over the next 250 million years.
In about one billion years the solar luminosity will be 10% higher, causing the atmosphere to become a moist greenhouse and a runaway evaporation of the oceans.
Within the next 600 million years, the concentration of carbon dioxide will fall below the critical threshold of about 50 parts per million needed to sustain C3 photosynthesis.
The inner radius of Earth's solid inner core is expanding at an average rate of roughly 0.5 mm per year, and this process supplies nearly all the energy needed to power the dynamo.
Earth will most probably be absorbed by the Sun in about 7.5 billion years, after the Sun has entered the red giant phase.
Mount Vesuvius can be expected to erupt about 40 times over the next 1,000 years, and about 50 magnitude 9 earthquakes may be expected worldwide in that period.
Paul F. Hoffman predicted in 1992 that North and South America would advance across the Pacific Ocean and merge with Asia, forming a supercontinent he dubbed Amasia.

entities.name: Holocene extinction
entities.role: ongoing mass extinction of species during the present geological epoch, caused by habitat destruction, invasive species, poaching, and climate change

entities.name: Milankovitch theory
entities.role: theory predicting that glacial periods will continue at least until the Quaternary glaciation ends, driven by orbital eccentricity, axial tilt, and precession

entities.name: Quaternary glaciation
entities.role: ongoing ice age through which Earth is passing, with the present Holocene interglacial period within it

entities.name: Barringer Meteorite Crater
entities.role: crater in Flagstaff, Arizona, showing evidence of celestial impact upon Earth

entities.name: Horne foundry copper smelter
entities.role: copper smelter in Rouyn-Noranda, Canada, pictured as an example of human influence

entities.name: Paul F. Hoffman
entities.role: Canadian geologist of Harvard University who in 1992 predicted the continents would merge with Asia to form the supercontinent Amasia

entities.name: Roy Livermore
entities.role: researcher who in the 1990s calculated a scenario in which Antarctica migrates northward and East Africa and Madagascar collide with Asia

entities.name: Christopher Scotese
entities.role: scientist who mapped predicted continental motions several hundred million years into the future as part of the Paleomap Project

entities.name: Paleomap Project
entities.role: project in which Christopher Scotese and colleagues mapped predicted future motions of the continents

entities.name: Peter D. Ward and Donald Brownlee
entities.role: authors of The Life and Death of Planet Earth, who argued some form of animal life may continue after most plant life disappears

entities.name: The Life and Death of Planet Earth
entities.role: book by Peter D. Ward and Donald Brownlee arguing that some animal life may persist after plant life is gone

entities.name: Pangaea Ultima
entities.role: future supercontinent expected to form in about 250 million years, with the Pacific Ocean stretching across half the planet

entities.name: San Andreas Fault
entities.role: fault along which about five to seven earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater are expected in the next 1,000 years

entities.name: Mount Rushmore
entities.role: sculptures that may still survive in some form after a million years

entities.name: Giza Necropolis
entities.role: site of pyramids that may still survive in some form after a million years

entities.name: Burgess Shale
entities.role: fossil site in British Columbia, Canada, used to determine the climate of the Cambrian Explosion
